{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABc3RPjA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhGZZ2Y", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 223, "title": "Redesign extension Live UI to match Concept A: compact controls, Graph Actions, and reading-first tabs", "body": "## Goal / visual direction

Implement the **first generated Live UI mockup (“Concept A”)** chosen by the user, not Concepts B or C. It is a **light, calm, reading-first** design with a white rounded app surface, subtle gray-lavender backgrounds, purple accent, restrained borders/shadows, compact recording controls, a distinct Graph Actions band, and a **large tabbed text reading area**.

The design reference appeared as the *first image* in the product-design conversation on 2026-11-05. Because that image is not attached to this GitHub issue, **this specification is self-contained**; implementers must not depend on accessing the conversation image.

**Critical:** this is a layout/visual redesign of the **existing Chrome extension Live screen**, not a new pipeline or source/output model. Preserve the generic graph-driven features and existing behavior.

## Target hierarchy (top → bottom)

```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ [waveform icon]  Live                   [Graph] [Models]    │
│                                                            │
│ [● Recording / current session state]                      │
│ [▶ Start]              [■ Stop]              [× Cancel]    │
│                                                            │
│ ┌ Graph Actions ─────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ [Button label from graph] [Another graph Button...]    │ │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                            │
│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│ │ [文字起こし]       [翻訳]          [要約]               │ │
│ ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │
│ │                                                        │ │
│ │   Readable text content of selected input tab          │ │
│ │   (majority of available Live screen height)           │ │
│ │                                                        │ │
│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│ [● status]  [current available model/processing info]      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 1. Header and recording controls

- A clean top row with small decorative waveform/app icon (CSS/SVG already in project or a small inline graphic; no dependency on a new icon package), prominent `Live` title, and **preserved** usable links to Graph Editor and Models. Do not introduce inert pin/ellipsis icons merely because they appear in the illustration.
- Place the *actual* session state in a compact colored status pill below/near the title: recording/running may show a red dot; starting/loading/stopping, idle, completed/canceled and errors must have distinct **truthful** states. Do not always display “Recording”.
- Arrange existing Start / Stop / Cancel controls in one intentional row with matching heights, generous hit areas and clear primary/secondary hierarchy. Use real disabled states: **Start must not look actionable during an active recording**, and Stop/Cancel must reflect actual supported state. Never alter their semantics.
- Avoid excessive top padding or duplicated diagnostic/status lines in the default view.

### 2. Graph Actions as a compact separate band

- Under recording controls, add/retain the rounded, very subtly tinted **Graph Actions** grouping seen in Concept A.
- Populate controls **dynamically from existing Button source nodes / graph actions**, preserving user-configured captions, per-node identity, disabled/busy states, accessibility and click dispatch established in #219.
- Example captions in the mockup (e.g. “Generate summary” and “Save snapshot”) are **illustrative only**. Do not hard-code action buttons or implement a new Save Snapshot feature in this issue. Render only actions actually present in the active graph.
- If the active graph has no Button nodes, collapse/hide the empty Graph Actions band cleanly.
- Make the band wrap adaptively on narrow windows without causing overflow; preserve action status/error messages in a compact, accessible way.

### 3. Main text area: dominant, single selected input tab

- Use the large, understated, white rounded reading card with a tidy tab strip, fine separators and **one tasteful purple active-tab underline**, as in Concept A. Tabs should not appear as unrelated stacked cards.
- Preserve the corrected Display behavior from #216: **one Display's input1…inputN ports are its switchable tabs**; one selected input's content is visible at a time. **Do not** change the contract to one Display per tab, or show different inputs in columns or stacked vertically.
- Use each input's existing user-configurable tab label; illustrations “文字起こし / 翻訳 / 要約” are not hardcoded product semantics.
- Content begins directly below tab strip; **no duplicate content heading, no Copy text button**, consistent with #221.
- Give the reading pane the majority of available visual height (not a tiny fixed card with the page mostly consumed by controls). Comfortable font size, line height, spacing, contrast and text measure; scroll text independently so recording controls and tabs remain easy to access.
- Retain literal TEXT and ITEM / keyed-pair/list display behavior; the mockup's timestamp badges / paragraph separators are **visual examples only** and must not imply synthetic timestamps or changed data semantics. If real data contains meaningful timestamps, it may be styled appropriately, but never invent them.
- Preserve per-tab scroll positions, near-bottom autoscroll, hidden-tab updates, DOM reuse, user text selection, empty content state, responsive wrapping, keyboard arrows/Home/End and accessible ARIA tab/tabpanel links.
- Keep multiple separate Display nodes usable under the pre-existing semantics, but optimize the common single Display experience. Avoid inventing a new cross-Display tab hierarchy.

### 4. Bottom status / diagnostics

- Replace the impression of a dense, always-visible diagnostics wall with a **compact bottom status strip**, visually subordinate to the reading pane. Use subtle dividers/chips for **real** existing session state (e.g., active/idle, elapsed time *only if actually tracked*, active model *only if verifiable*, etc.).
- **Do not hardcode “GPT-4o”, “Runtime: 00:01:32” or other mockup sample data**. This extension is local-first and supports multiple models; the UI must reflect actual model/session state, or omit unavailable fields.
- Preserve errors, model-recovery guidance, active-graph-change warning, target authorization, detailed diagnostics and audio/TTS controls. Keep urgent/actionable notices visible; move optional or verbose details into accessible disclosure areas where sensible. Do not hide real failures just for visual cleanliness.
- Avoid a fixed bottom overlay that obscures text or traps scrolling. Ensure the status area and reading region are usable with tall/short Live windows.

## Visual styling

- Apply a **cohesive light theme to Live** similar to Concept A: off-white outer surface, white reading panel, pale-gray/lavender action band, subtle 1px outlines, soft restrained shadows, approx. 10–16px corner radii, and purple active/primary accents. Keep status red/green only for actual meaning.
- Consistent vertical rhythm and aligned panel edges; typography optimized for Japanese text and long English translation paragraphs.
- Prefer existing CSS and icons; no gratuitous library or animation. Respect reduced-motion preference and visible focus. Maintain WCAG-appropriate contrast.
- Scope style changes to the Live page so **Graph Editor and Models are not unintentionally recolored or broken** by existing shared `extension/recorder.css` selectors.
- Responsive desktop, medium-width Live window, and ~390px narrow viewport with usable 44px-ish control targets, no page-width overflow, sensible action wrapping, and no giant empty header area.

## Existing implementation to inspect

- `extension/recorder.html`: header/nav, `.capture-panel`, `.recording-heading`, `#graph-action-area`, diagnostics, `#live-displays`, speaker output.
- `extension/recorder.css`: global dark theme variables/shared styling, Live controls, Graph Actions layout, tab strip and `.display-content` (`max-height: 52dvh` currently limits reading area).
- `extension/recorder.js`: session state, buttons, Graph Actions rendering, error/diagnostic visibility and tab rendering.
- `extension/live-text-regions.js`: per-Display input tabs, hidden updates, scroll intent and pane DOM.
- Existing MV3/Playwright Live/Display/Graph Actions tests; update docs/help only where UI descriptions change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **Concept A visual hierarchy** appears in Live: refined Live header → truthful session pill + Start/Stop/Cancel → compact Graph Actions band if present → dominant reading panel with purple-underlined tabs → compact accurate status/diagnostic area.
- [ ] The content reading area occupies substantially more of the usable window than metadata/chrome, and remains readable and scrollable while transcription updates.
- [ ] Input ports of a **single Display** remain separate switchable tabs, with no duplicated pane title or Copy text button.
- [ ] Existing Button nodes dynamically populate Graph Actions; no hardcoded “Save snapshot” or other fake features.
- [ ] State and model/runtime text is based on real session data; no fake model name, fabricated timer, or incorrect “Recording” badge when idle/stopped.
- [ ] Graph Editor/Models navigation, real errors/recovery, target selection, audio/TTS UI and graph saving/session semantics are preserved.
- [ ] Active/inactive tab updates, scroll preservation, keyboard/touch tabs, action buttons, Stop/Cancel/Start, accessibility and no-display/single-tab states still work.
- [ ] Visual snapshots/screenshots and browser/packaged MV3 tests are produced at desktop, typical Live-window and ~390px widths; no horizontal overflow, unreadable controls or hidden actionable errors.
- [ ] Confirm light-theme visual regression does not affect Graph Editor/Models; list tests actually executed and any unverified cases.

## Scope guardrails

This task is **Live UI/UX styling and layout**, with minimal state-derived view-model updates where necessary. Do not modify node semantics, pipelines, model loading, graph schema, Display tab mappings, or create new graph actions solely to match the illustration.

Related: #216 (Display input tabs), #219 (Graph Actions), #221 (remove duplicate tab headings/Copy text).
